parts.text: Which claim correctly classifies a fluid?

options.text: Water and air are fluids because they flow and do not keep a fixed shape.
Sand is a fluid because it can be poured into a jar.
Only liquids are fluids; gases are not fluids because they have no fixed volume.

parts.text: Give one reason for your choice.

stem: Rohan compares water in a bottle, air in the room, and dry sand poured into a jar.

part_answers.answer: Fluids are liquids and gases that flow and lack a fixed shape; pouring sand does not make the solid grains a fluid.

teacher.key_rationale: Liquids and gases are fluids because they flow and do not retain a fixed shape. Pourable sand is still a solid collection of grains; gases are fluids even though they lack fixed volume.
